domains.title: Domains
domains.description: Domains or URLs to search for contact details. One row is returned per domain, and only domains where a contact is found are charged.

startUrls.title: Start URLs (optional)
startUrls.description: Same thing in Apify's URL-list format, for chaining after another actor. Merged with `domains`.

concurrency.title: Concurrency
concurrency.description: How many domains to crawl at once. 15 is a good default; raising it does not reduce cost, because cost follows total runtime.

maxPagesPerDomain.title: Maximum pages per domain
maxPagesPerDomain.description: Crawling stops as soon as both an email and a phone number are found, so most domains use one or two pages of this budget.

timeoutMs.title: Per-request timeout (ms)
timeoutMs.description: A slow host is reported as unreachable rather than holding up the run. Raising this trades runtime for a few more slow sites.

domainBudgetMs.title: Per-domain budget (ms)
domainBudgetMs.description: Wall-clock cap for one domain across all its pages.

useProxy.title: Use Apify Proxy (datacenter)
useProxy.description: Strongly recommended. Measured on a 100-domain sample: six domains that answered a direct connection with 403 or nothing were reachable through rotating datacenter IPs.

allowInsecureTls.title: Read sites with an invalid certificate
allowInsecureTls.description: Small business sites let certificates expire. Only public pages are read and nothing is ever submitted, so the risk is bad data rather than exposed data.

defaultCountry.title: Default country for phone numbers
defaultCountry.description: ISO country code (GB, US, AU...) used as the fallback for local-format phone numbers. It applies only when the domain's ccTLD, the site's structured data and the page itself (its language region, a UK or Canadian postcode, the numbers on it) all fail to point to a country.

proxyGroups.title: Proxy groups (optional)
proxyGroups.description: Leave empty for Apify's default datacenter pool. Set ["RESIDENTIAL"] only if datacenter IPs are being blocked on your lists — residential traffic is billed per gigabyte.
